latest_wiki.summary: The text reports a 1994 attack against AMIA, the Jewish community building in Buenos Aires. Hezbollah is held responsible for it.

A car bomb exploded outside a Jewish community centre in London thirteen hours after a car bomb attack on the Israeli embassy, injuring 22 people. The date is derived from the text's statement that it occurred eight days after the AMIA attack.
A suicide attack drove a van loaded with explosives into the AMIA Jewish community center in Buenos Aires and detonated it, killing 85 people and injuring over 300.

Members of The Base spray-painted swastikas, the word Jude, and The Base's symbol on the outside of Beth Israel Sinai Congregation. The text places this during Operation Kristallnacht, which it dates to September 21.

Nathan Weeden spray-painted swastikas and The Base's symbol on the exterior of Temple Jacob. The text places this during Operation Kristallnacht, which it dates to September 21 in the body, though the lead gives September 19.

Abraham Surasky, a Jewish peddler, was shot and axed to death by Lee Green and George Toole in rural South Carolina about 15 miles from Aiken. Green's wife Dora was also involved, and the court acquitted Green of murder.

According to a sworn affidavit, Lee Green shot at and attempted to murder another Jewish peddler named Levy about three weeks before the murder of Abraham Surasky. The date and place are not given beyond this.

The text reports the Slánský show trial in Communist Czechoslovakia, in which 14 leading Communists were tried and convicted, most of them hanged. The text says the trial had an anti-Semitic thrust and that eleven of the fourteen defendants were Jews.

The text reports that between 29 July and 16 September 1941 the 454th Security Division captured about 1,500 civilians and Red Army soldiers, and that 78 of them, who were Jews, were killed. The text names occupied Ukraine and Southern Russia as the area of operations.
The text reports that the Buergenthal family's resort hotel in Ľubochňa was confiscated by the Hlinka Guard in 1938 or early 1939. The text says the family owned and managed the hotel.

The text reports that in November 1938 a pogrom across Germany, known as Kristallnacht, followed the assassination of a German diplomat. Synagogues were burned, Jewish homes and businesses were attacked, thousands of Jews were arrested, and some were stoned or beaten to death.
The text reports that members of the division executed eighteen escaped prisoners between 7 and 11 April 1945. The location is not named.

latest_jta.summary: The article reports that a Russian monarchist paper in Brazil, the Russian Gazette, published an article making insulting accusations against Jews. The local Jewish community has taken steps against those thought responsible.
The article reports that Jews in suburban towns of Ontario received letters signed by Swastika clubs warning them to leave their homes.
Members of the Polish Nazi Party in Lodz paraded the streets, stood outside Jewish shops and tried to stop customers from entering.

The article reports that the St. Edouard section of the Federation of Fascist Labor Clubs adopted a resolution calling for a complete stop to Jewish immigration, and forwarded it to the immigration minister at Ottawa.
The article reports that Professor Theodor Lessing, a German Jewish philosopher and refugee from Germany, was killed on Czechoslovak territory, and that police are hunting his assassins.
The article reports serious riots on August 16 and 17 in Willowvale Park in Toronto, which it links to the Swastika activity against Jews.
Theodor Lessing, a German-Jewish philosopher and refugee from Nazi Germany, was shot dead in his bedroom at his villa in Marienbad by two men firing through the window. Police searched for a suspect.
Theodor Lessing had received letters threatening his life about three weeks before his murder, according to the Prague press. One letter warned he would be dead within a month.
Purple-shirted Nazi news vendors in Katowice attacked Jewish passersby, and repeated fights occurred there.

The article reports that the Quebec city council passed a resolution urging federal authorities not to relax immigration laws, and sent it to the federal immigration minister. The resolution said Jewish immigration would create a state within a state.

The article reports that Brazil's Ministry of Labor has stopped acknowledging affidavits submitted by Jews to bring family members into the country, so Jewish immigration has nearly ceased. The article says Germans, and a police chief described as anti-Semitic, are said to be behind it.
The article reports that Nazi headquarters at Magdeburg issued orders to members not to buy from or deal with Jews, and warned that offenders would be expelled from the party.
The article reports that youths pasted swastikas on fences and tombstones at Jewish cemeteries on Roselawn Avenue in Toronto, during the month of Elul.

Polish anti-Semites painted all the Jewish shops in Nowobrodnow overnight with signs urging Poles not to buy from Jews and to beat them. The article also reports that leaflets calling for confiscation of Jewish property and a boycott of Jewish businesses were distributed the next morning.

latest_research.summary: The Observatory on Antisemitism in Belgium reports that a paving stone was thrown through a third-floor window of the Orthodox Jewish community synagogue in Anderlecht, shattering the glass. The Observatory describes it as vandalism targeting a Jewish place of worship, and the US ambassador calls it an antisemitic attack. The perpetrator is unidentified.

Jewish News reports that a woman was filmed describing Jewish people as "killers and psychopaths" during a protest outside Sheffield Town Hall. South Yorkshire Police first recorded a hate incident. A later Jewish News report says police concluded the remarks did not amount to a recordable crime, and the lower, no-crime finding is the one noted here.

Two unknown persons threw Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel synagogue complex on Brunnenstraße in Berlin-Mitte in the early morning. According to reports the devices landed on the pavement and no one was hurt.

A 26-year-old Jewish student wearing a kippah was struck on the head with a folding spade outside the Hohe Weide synagogue, according to the sources. Police assumed an antisemitic motive, and a later court ruling is reported to have found a targeted attack on a Jew.

Unknown persons scratched swastikas into several gravestones at the Jewish cemetery on Krankenhausstraße in Cloppenburg, and state security police investigated for incitement to hatred. Police later reported that two teenagers admitted the act.
Witnesses told police that a group of about 15 people gathered in front of the synagogue, shouted and burned an Israeli flag. State security police took over the investigation.

Police reported that a 24-year-old Jewish man was assaulted on a tram in Erfurt after another man noticed his Star of David necklace. The attacker tried to drag him off the tram, kicked him and later threatened him, and is being investigated for a politically motivated hate crime.

Berlin police reported that an unidentified man punched a 60-year-old man to the ground in a park after learning that he was Jewish, and the victim had minor facial injuries. State security police are investigating suspected aggravated assault with an antisemitic motive.
Unknown persons damaged the glass of the synagogue entrance door with stones, and police found a partly burned Israeli flag in front of it, according to the reports. Three suspects were arrested.

About 180 people moved from the station forecourt toward the synagogue in an unregistered rally, and antisemitic chants were shouted, according to a press report. Church bodies described the events near the synagogue as antisemitic riots.

RIAS reports that a resident of an asylum shelter in Coburg attacked another resident with a knife because he took him for a Jew. The Coburg prosecutor's office is reported to have assumed the perpetrator was not criminally responsible.

The entrance door of a residential house in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg was sprayed with a Star of David. State security police investigated on suspicion of incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung), and the press reported that the marking apparently aimed to intimidate Jewish residents.
